title: Runway Extension & Hiring Triggers Playbook (Aug planning)
body:
Purpose:
This is a pragmatic playbook for extending runway via hiring levers and targeted pricing responses under three price-demand shock scenarios. Intended audience: CFO, Head of Finance, HR, and GTM leads. This is a working sheet — numbers are high-level and intended for planning discussions, not final board materials.

Overview / short version:
- Define three shock scenarios (mild / moderate / severe). For each scenario, map a phased hiring plan (pause, selective freeze, reductions), identify quick cost levers (pricing experiments, deferred capex, vendor renegotiation), and estimate 6-month burn and runway impact.
- We prioritize preserving customer-facing SLA/Redeployment spend (Dedicated & Private infra) and product availability. Hiring cuts prioritize non-customer-facing functions first, followed by slower ramp in applied ML and platform engineering if needed.

Scenarios (assumptions):
1) Mild shock — elastic demand: -7% net revenue vs plan across 6 months.
   - Assumptions: slower new customer additions, existing churn up 1.5ppt, pricing pressure on new annual contracts.
   - Actions: immediate hiring freeze for non-critical IC roles (60% of open reqs), pause non-essential headcount (contractors), push hiring for SRE and infra that enable revenue (no layoffs).
2) Moderate shock — structural slowdown: -18% revenue vs plan across 6 months.
   - Assumptions: deeper churn, longer sales cycles; new pricing discounting required to close deals.
   - Actions: freeze all new external hiring; convert some open roles to deferred status; 8–12 week voluntary separation package offer for selected non-customer groups; targeted 5–10% salary reprioritization for senior IC hiring.
3) Severe shock — demand collapse: -35%+ revenue vs plan over 6 months.
   - Assumptions: macro-induced demand collapse; enterprise renewals delayed or revised.
   - Actions: structured headcount reductions up to 12–18% of FTEs, prioritizing central ops and non-core GTM programs; temporary pause on new product expansions and major capex; immediate price re-calibration playbook and emergency deal review committee.

Phased hiring trigger matrix (example rules):
- Trigger A (Green): trailing 3-month revenue >= 95% of plan => No hire freezes; proceed with planned hires.
- Trigger B (Amber): trailing 3-month revenue 85–95% => Pause non-revenue hires; only mission-critical backfills approved by TRiage committee.
- Trigger C (Red): trailing 3-month revenue < 85% => Full external hiring freeze + compensation reductions for contractors; execute Phase 1 reductions if runway < 9 months.

High-level modeled impact (illustrative):
- Starting monthly net burn (baseline) : $5.2M
- Mild shock (immediate levers) : reduce burn to $4.6M (runway + 3 months)
- Moderate shock (freeze + modest reductions) : reduce burn to $3.9M (runway + 6 months)
- Severe shock (reductions + pricing + deferred capex) : reduce burn to $2.8M (runway + 10+ months)

Simple 6-month sensitivity table (illustrative numbers):
| Scenario  | Avg monthly revenue | Avg monthly burn | Runway months (assumes $60M cash) | Priority hiring areas kept |
|----------|---------------------:|-----------------:|-------------------------------:|---------------------------|
| Baseline | $18.5M              | $5.2M            | 11.5                           | All planned hires          |
| Mild     | $17.2M (-7%)        | $4.6M            | 13.0                           | SRE, Sales AE top hires    |
| Moderate | $15.2M (-18%)       | $3.9M            | 15.4                           | Customer success, core infra |
| Severe   | $12.0M (-35%)       | $2.8M            | 21.4                           | Critical SLA only (no expansion) |

Role-level sequencing (who we pause / keep):
- Keep: SRE, Core Serving Runtime, Frontline support (CS Tier 1), Key account AMs for top 25 customers
- Defer: New GTM programs (events, new SDR hires), non-critical infra tools, general engineering expansions not tied to revenue
- Target for reduction: discretionary headcount (marketing campaigns, open product research reqs), older contractor engagements, duplicate IC roles from tooling consolidation

Cost-saving levers (ranked by speed to effect):
1) Hiring freeze / contractor pause (fast, high impact)
2) Vendor renegotiation & deferred invoices (30–60 days)
3) Stretching capex (delay major hardware refresh by 1–2 quarters)
4) Targeted pricing increases for new sign-ups + stricter discount approvals (requires GTM alignment)
5) Temporary hiring-level compensation freezes or deferrals (notify in advance to limit morale impact)

Communications & HR pathways:
- Draft FAQ and manager scripting for hiring freeze and voluntary separation + severance ranges (1–3 months base for voluntary program).
- Legal and compliance to review severance offers and benefits continuation.
- Prep candidate pipeline pause note and recruiter directives.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Threshold for converting voluntary separations into involuntary layoffs if take rate is below 18% (finance recommendation: convert after 6 weeks).
- Exact savings target per percentage point of headcount reduction by function (need HR run-rate data).
- Which customer segments get protected discounts vs which see stricter price discipline.

Back-of-envelope sensitivity example (single-variable):
- Each 1% reduction in total FTEs ~ $0.18M monthly run-rate savings (includes benefits and associated cost). So a 10% reduction => ~ $1.8M/mo.

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- These are intentionally conservative in GTM hiring protection; product roadmap pushes may be paused but we preserve core delivery.
- Need tighter burndown model by role — Finance to request HR export of headcount-by-role with loaded cost (pay + eq) for FY25/26.
- Recommend next steps: build a live sheet (linked to payroll export), and run Monte Carlo on mixed shock outcomes with probability weights.

Attachments / next steps:
- Action owner assignments: Ethan (finance) => create live model; Sofia (HR) => prepare voluntary separation package draft; Aisha (GTM) => pricing experiment plan and fast-review committee; Noah (Legal) => severance T&Cs.
- Follow-up meeting scheduled: Finance ops sync, 2026-03-16, 10:00 PST (tentative).

End of playbook (working doc).
